verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission is a crewed moon mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "3 NASA astronauts and a Canadian astronaut will venture around the moon" (R1); "NASA's long-anticipated Artemis 2 mission — the first crewed flight around the moon" (R2); "A crew of four astronauts is scheduled to lift off" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly describe Artemis 2 as a crewed mission flying around the moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Next launch is Artemis II from Kennedy Space Center on Wednesday, April 1, 2026" (R1); "NASA is officially targeting Wednesday (April 1)" (R2); "lift off at 6:24 p.m. on April 1" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm the scheduled launch date as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 launch is scheduled for 6:24 p.m. EDT (2224 GMT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Launch: 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, 2026" (R1); "lift off at 6:24 p.m. EDT (2224 GMT)" (R2); "lift off at 6:24 p.m." (R3); "At 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state the exact time and time zone conversion.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 launch is from Launch Pad 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Launch location: Launch Pad 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center near Cape Canaveral, Florida" (R1); "Pad 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center (KSC) in Florida" (R2); "NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Direct matches for pad, center, and location.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission carries four astronauts around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "send four astronauts further in space"; "3 NASA astronauts and a Canadian astronaut" (R1); "send four astronauts on a roughly 10-day journey around the moon" (R2); "A crew of four astronauts" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as four astronauts on a lunar flyby/orbit mission.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission duration is approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "10-day flight" (R1); "roughly 10-day journey" (R2); "10-day journey" (R3); "10-day journey" (R4); "10-day Artemis 2 mission" (R5)

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission has a two-hour launch window opening at 6:24 p.m.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, 2026, with a two-hour window" (R1); "2-hour window for the launch, so it could lift off anytime between 6:24 p.m. and 8:24 p.m." (R2); "three two-hour windows ... starting with between 6:24 p.m. ET" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm two-hour window opening at 6:24 p.m.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 launch window is 6:24 p.m. – 8:24 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "between 6:24 p.m. and 8:24 p.m. EDT" (R2); "6:24 p.m. ET and 8:24 p.m. ET on April 1" (R3); "April 1: 6:24 p.m. – 8:24 p.m. ET" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Exact window times and ET specified in sources.

verifications.claim: The official NASA YouTube channel will provide a live stream starting with fueling operations at 7:45 a.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "7:45 a.m. EDT (1145 GMT): Fueling coverage of the SLS rocket with NASA commentary"; "NASA ... on its own website and NASA+ streaming service, and YouTube."
verifications.reasoning: R2 specifies fueling coverage at 7:45 a.m. EDT as part of NASA livestreams including YouTube; high confidence despite not explicitly 'official NASA YouTube' phrasing.

verifications.claim: As of March 31, 2026, there is an 80% chance of favorable conditions for the Artemis 2 launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "As of Tuesday, March 31, all signs are looking positive" (R1); "80% chance that it will be a go" for April 1 (R3); "weather forecast for launch day shows an 80% chance of favourable weather conditions" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources around March 31 cite 80% favorable weather for launch.

verifications.claim: Backup launch windows for Artemis 2 are available from April 2 through April 6.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "launch windows available daily from April 1 to April 6" (R2); "second window ... on April 2 ... final available window of this week ... on April 3" (R3); lists April 2 through April 6 (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm backup windows through April 6.
